fixes.explanation: Enemies would make for an easier announcement, I'll give you that. But the verse never mentions enemies. God says to declare “…to My people their transgression and to the house of Jacob their sins.” (Isaiah 58:1) The ram's horn is how loud the voice should be, and the message is for His own people.

A thank-you would've sounded a lot nicer, friend. The verse says something else, though: “…you oppress all your workers.” (Isaiah 58:3) I think this one hurts, because the workers are being pressed down on the very day of the fast.
You know that feeling of being left on hold, friend? The verse says something different: “Then you will call, and the LORD will answer…” (Isaiah 58:9) There's no waiting in that line. He answers.

Test is a sneaky guess, friend, and I see you, but the verse doesn't go there. God says “Then you will call, and the LORD will answer…” (Isaiah 58:9) Remember, they had asked why He didn't notice them. Here He promises that when they call, He answers, no quiz required.
Noonday, friend. God says “…your night will be like noonday.” (Isaiah 58:10) Noon is the brightest part of the day. So the promise is a night that's like the middle of the day.

Midnight is already the night, friend. So it can't be the promise. God says “…your night will be like noonday.” (Isaiah 58:10) Noon is the brightest part of the day, and that's what their night is compared to.

That's it. God says “You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.” (Isaiah 58:11) Picture a garden in a sun-scorched land, and a spring whose waters never fail. That's a lot of comfort in one verse.

That's the pair, friend. God says “you will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of the Streets of Dwelling.” (Isaiah 58:12) A breach is a gap or a break. The verse also says they will rebuild the ancient ruins and restore the age-old foundations.

Mystery sounds exciting, friend, but that's not the word. God says “…if you call the Sabbath a delight, and the LORD’s holy day honorable…” (Isaiah 58:13) The word is delight. It's a very different feeling from a puzzle to solve.
